title: ProtoRAIL: A Risk-cognizant Imitation Agent for Adaptive vCPU Oversubscription In the Cloud
problem: Cloud vCPU oversubscription policies must jointly minimize overloading risk (hot nodes) and maximize utilization (stranded resource recovery), but demand patterns vary dynamically across VM types and time, making static heuristic policies either too conservative (waste capacity) or too aggressive (cause overload).
motivation: Online RL cannot safely train on live cloud infrastructure and struggles to converge with two competing objectives (COGS benefit vs overloading risk). Supervised learning is unaware of environment interactions. Imitation learning from offline telemetry is feasible, but noisy data leads to sub-optimal policies. Prototypical IL exploits approximate symmetries in usage patterns across VM/service types, and active feedback from domain experts can de-risk policies without requiring online interaction.
method: ProtoRAIL encodes CPU usage sequences using a neural network (LSTM or Transformer) into embeddings, then groups them into K prototypes representing typical VM behavior; oversubscription decisions are made by comparing how similar current usage is to each prototype. It learns from expert decisions via imitation learning (behavior cloning or adversarial training) while pursuing four goals: keeping prototypes close to real data, far apart from each other, grounded in actual trajectories for interpretability, and good at predicting actual demand. When it encounters uncertain situations (mixed or overlapping prototypes) or risky predictions (predicted oversubscription below actual usage), it asks domain experts to vote on prototypes, suggest actions, or restructure clusters (merge/split), then automatically adjusts how strongly each training goal is weighted to apply this feedback—only requesting help when genuinely uncertain or risky.
key_novelty: Interpretable prototype-based imitation learning where experts can minimize risk by voting on and restructuring pattern clusters, requiring minimal feedback queries.
contributions: Prototypical imitation learning framework for oversubscription ratio prediction using usage trajectory equivalence classes
Prototype diversity, representativeness, and interpretability regularization in a unified loss
Active KITL query framework minimizing expert budget via uncertainty + risk-based triggering
Advice potential gates (exponential loss scaling) for infusing prototype/action feedback
Deployment on Microsoft internal cloud: 9.4% vCPU utilization improvement, 0% hot node rate
Generalization to airline ticket overbooking domain

metrics.hot_node_rate: 0% hot node rate (vs 0.89-1.47% for baselines including Coop-MARL, GAIL, BC, DDPG)
metrics.remain_core_benefit: 8161 remain cores vs 7938 for best baseline (Dagger with 20 human steps)
metrics.deployment_utilization: 9.4% vCPU utilization improvement on Microsoft internal cloud
metrics.deployment_hot_nodes: 0% hot node rate on 300 deployed clusters
metrics.kitl_query_budget: <=10 total feedback queries to reach stable performance
metrics.benefit_risk_ratio: BRR 31.34 vs 18.95 for heuristics and 7.79 for manual

limitations: Prototype count K must be tuned; wrong K causes redundant or missing coverage of usage patterns
Active KITL requires human experts with domain knowledge; LLMs are inferior (87% vs 98% clustering accuracy)
Bootstrap period needed before alpha tuning and KITL convergence
Airline ticket overbooking shows performance degradation due to COVID-19 distribution shift
